Hi Neha — thanks for the recap. Security has a short checklist before we move to procurement: 

- SOC 2 Type II report (full report or SOC2 + bridge letter) — required
- Signed BAA — required
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest — required; key management options?
- Detailed audit logging (admin + data access) and retention policy — required; ability to export logs to our SIEM?
- Data residency: US-only hosting for PHI — required
- Network isolation: Preference for Private VPC or Dedicated (no shared tenant) — Private VPC preferred if feasible; Dedicated acceptable with strict tenancy controls
- Support for audits: ability to provide evidence and work with our auditors during vendor assessment — required

Can you confirm Redwood’s support on all the above and share the SOC2 and BAA (we received the redacted SOC2 from your attachment but would like the full report and an estimated timeline for getting a signed BAA)? Also can you confirm if Redwood provides HSM/KMS integration options for customer-managed keys?

We’re aiming to make a decision within the next 3 weeks, so a technical deep-dive early next week would be ideal. Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Partnerships, Elara Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up (HIPAA / SOC2 / BAA)

Hi Alex — copying in Rishi (Sr. Solutions) to cover technical details. Quick answers below and proposed next steps.

1) SOC2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II for our production control environment. Full report can be shared under NDA / RDC — attached is the non-redacted report for review.
2) BAA: We fully support signing a BAA for PHI workloads. I’ve attached a draft BAA (BAA-draft-Redwood.docx) for your legal team; we can iterate. Typical timeline to sign: ~2–3 weeks depending on redlines.
3) Encryption/KMS: TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 at rest. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private VPC options; Hosted API has Redwood-managed keys but we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private setups.
4) Audit logs: We provide admin + data access logs; retention is configurable (default 90 days). Logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure S3 export or push to your logging endpoint (we’ll include sample config).
5) Data residency: We can deploy in US-only regions. For strict residency and network isolation we recommend Private VPC (on your cloud account) or a Dedicated cluster in a region you control.
6) Network isolation & tenancy: Private VPC = customer VPC peering / PrivateLink / no shared tenant. Dedicated = isolated hardware pools with strict tenancy controls; both meet your preference but Private VPC is preferred for the highest isolation.
7) Audit support: We support auditor access patterns and will coordinate evidence packages; for on-prem audits we will allow agreed-upon evidence sharing per the BAA and NDA.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll share links to the redacted SOC2 (attached) and the full report under NDA — Neha will send the DocuSign/DocSend link for the NDA.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive w/ Rishi and your security team to walk the network diagram and KMS options — suggested times: Mon 2026-03-09 09:00–11:00 PT or Tue 2026-03-10 14:00–16:00 PT.
- If Private VPC is required, we’ll send the Private VPC network diagram and implementation checklist (attached: private-vpc-network-diagram.pdf) and a high-level runbook for provisioning.

I’ve attached the following for your review: SOC2-report-Redwood-2025.pdf (full), BAA-draft-Redwood.docx, private-vpc-network-diagram.pdf. If you prefer, we can open a narrow NDA first and exchange the full SOC2 over DocSend.

Best — Marissa
